case_name: State of Mysore and Others v K. Chandrasekhara Adiga and Another
respondent:
K. Chandrasekhara Adiga and Another
Supreme Court of India

28 January 1976
C.A. No. 2444 of 1968 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 27 May 1968 of the Mysore High Court in W.P. No. 2381 of 1965).
The Judgment was delivered by: SARKARIA, J.
1.  This appeal on certificate is directed against a judgment of the High Court of Mysore allowing a petition filed u/art. 226 of the Constitution by the respondent whereby the impugned condition attached to the assignment of &'Kumki&' land made in favour of respondent No. 1, was quashed.

facts: The district of South Kanara was, before the reorganization of States in 1956, a part of the State of Madras.
Warga formed prior to Fasli year 1276 (corresponding to 1886 A.D.) are termed as &'kadim warg&' lands and the Government-owned waste lands within 100 yards of such wargs, are called &'kumki lands&'.
Owners of the &'warg&' lands enjoy certain privileges in respect of &'kumki&' lands.
The kumkidar has a preferential claim for assignment of the &'kumki&' land subject to predominant public interest.
Respondent No. 1, here in was a registered holder of &'kadim warg&' lands survey Nos. 90/8/90/9, 8, 22, 24 etc. of Kakkunji village under kadim kumki right.
On August 2, 1961, respondent No. 1 made an application to the Tehsildar, Udipi for assignment of this kumki land, admeasuring 7.34 acres, in survey Nos. 134/2 and 134/3.
issues: Whether the condition attached to the order of assignment is violative of Arts. 19 and 31 of the Constitution.
Whether a kumkidar has a fundamental proprietary right in the kumki lands.
Whether the Government was competent to curtail or take away the privileges of the kumkidar by an executive order.
petitioner_arguments: (i) The High Court was wrong in holding that the assignment of kumki lands in South Kanara district is not governed by the Land Grant Rules, 1960.
(ii) A kumkidar has no idefeasible right of property in the kumki lands which vest in the State Government.
(iii) If the government order dated March 17, 1964 was an executive order, so were the standing orders of the Revenue Board under which the kumki rights are claimed.
(iv) In any case, the order dated March 17, 1964 does not take away or abridge any property rights of kumkidar.
respondent_arguments: A kumkidar has a substantial interest and rights in the kumki lands. These rights though described as &'privileges&' in the standing orders of the Madras Board of Revenue and the rules framed u/s. 26 of the Madras Forest Act, are rights of &'property&' within the contemplation of Arts. 19 and 31 of the Constitution.
court_reasoning: The High Court was wrong in holding that the assignment of kumki lands is not governed by the Land Grant Rules, 1960.
A kumkidar has no idefeasible right of property in the kumki lands which vest in the State Government.

Even if the condition restricting the right of the kumkidar to the trees on the assigned land was invalid, the High Court should have quashed the entire order of assignment and remitted the case to the tehsildar for reconsideration.
holding: The impugned condition attached to the order of assignment is violative of Arts. 19 and 31 of the Constitution.
The Government could not curtail, abridge or take away the privileges of the kumkidar by a mere executive order, as distinguished from a valid law.
